The Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Jaro Egbo, and five other individuals for questioning over the deadly violence in Uduere community, Delta State. The invitations followed a shooting incident during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, on Monday. The police also disclosed that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited the community on Tuesday for an on-the-spot assessment of the incident. The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, Bright Edafe, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the invitations were part of efforts to establish the involvement of those connected with the incident. The statement listed Omo-Agege as the first person invited, directing him to report at the Delta State Police Command Headquarters, Asaba, on Thursday, November 26, at 11am. Egbo is expected to appear at 2pm on the same day. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The five other individuals invited are Gowon Egoide, former Chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent Youth Chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide from Otowvodo; Erukaye Egoide, his nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate. They are scheduled to report at the police headquarters on Friday, November 27, at noon. “The invitations form part of ongoing investigations aimed at establishing their level of involvement in the incident,” the statement said. The command urged all those invited to honour their appointments and cooperate with investigators, warning that supporters and other persons not specifically invited would not be allowed to accompany them. 2027: SDP demands equal police protection for all parties Omo-Agege rejects judgment nullifying senatorial ticket, vows to appeal Delta campaign killings: Oborevwori orders arrest of perpetrators “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, urges all invited persons to honour the invitations as scheduled and cooperate fully with the Police while noting that the invitations are to the mentioned individuals only as the Command will not accept the presence of supporters and other persons not explicitly invited,” the statement said. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice irrespective of political affiliation or status. “The CP further appeals to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as the investigation progresses,” the statement added. PUNCH Online reported that gunfire erupted on Monday, during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege to Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area, leaving several people dead and others injured. The Nigeria Police Force’s preliminary report put the death toll at six. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation initially reported four deaths, including two of the senator’s aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, and described the incident as an assassination attempt on the former deputy senate president. However, Egbo accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three people were killed. The conflicting accounts of the incident are expected to form part of the issues to be examined during the police investigation. Following the violence, the Delta State Government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area.
